newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank says to keep yuan stable in '97.
newsitem.headline: China central bank says to keep yuan stable in '97.

text.p: China's central bank plans to intervene to keep the yuan from appreciating further in 1997 and sees foreign reserves swelling as a result, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The yuan would remain stable this year despite mounting pressure to appreciate, the newspaper quoted Tao Liming, deputy director of the International Finance Research Institute under the central bank, the People's Bank of China, as saying.
He cited several factors that would keep pressure on the yuan to strengthen this year.
The gap between supply and demand of the yuan would persist because of a central bank decision to retain moderately tight monetary policy in 1997, he said.
Although credit may ease slightly in 1997, the rise in investment would soak up all additional capital, he said.

He cited robust growth in foreign investment as another factor. Foreign direct investment, which exceeded $40 billion last year, would indirectly expand the supply of foreign currency by providing the foreign exchange to finance imports, he said, but did not elaborate.
In addition, the central bank would not let the yuan appreciate to prevent an impact on exports, Tao said.
He forecast China's gross domestic product would reach 7,500 billion yuan ($903 billion) in 1997, with about $160 billion coming from foreign trade -- nearly one-sixth of the total.
